Abandoned Babies

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The growing crisis abandoned babies, a woman's drive to address this human tragedy

Summary:
How to tell the story of babies who are abandoned at birth.

The Child Protection Activist
The plight of abandoned babies in South Africa is an issue that the government does not want to deal and are pushing under the carpet…says Dee Blackie, child protection activist. It all started for Dee when she saw picture in a newspaper of a little girl who had been abandoned and died on the outskirts of Soweto. Dee knew she had to do something. Approaching the government she was told:
 “don’t understand” the problem ..I went back to university to do my masters in Anthropology looking child abandonment and adoption in the context of African ancestral beliefs.

….the abandoned
Sindisiwe, whose name means ‘saved’ was abandoned by her mother in a hospital toilet, she was found by a nurse who thought she was dead, until miraculously Sindisiwe coughed and took her first breath. The nurse rushed her to the neonatal unit in the hospital and that is where she stayed for several months. Sindisiwe was eventually raised by her grandparents until they died when Sindisiwe was 12, and later by aunts. Sindisiwe never knew who her mother was until years later when she was an adult but on confronting her was “ I wish you had died then” Sindi, now in her 30’s, works as a charismatic minister ministering to people around the country. She is in the process of being ordained and setting up her own ministry. In Dee’s word’s “In her quiet unassuming way is an inspiration to many.”

….the saviours

Nicole and Johan Olivier are a family of five, their youngest Noah was abandoned at birth, he was left under a tree in a field outside a township wrapped in a plastic bag inside his mother jacket. Nicole Olivier who had just miscarried twins got a call about Noah, for her it was meant to be. Love at first sight and three weeks later she adopted him, He is now the happiest and bubbliest 4 year old and the Olivier’s could not imagine their family without him.


Further information:
“My husband, Jeremy, is a professional musician and singer-songwriter here in South Africa. We often write together, and about a year ago, we felt inspired to write about our story: how two tragic events have been turned into something so beautiful.
“The response to this song has truly overwhelmed us. Jeremy has performed it on stages in Holland and Switzerland, as well as here in our own country and it seems to move people deeply.
The Olivier’s work for UNICEF SA and the issue of abandoned babies is very close to their heart.
“We are currently working with UNICEF SA on a new campaign called ‘Ending Violence Against Children and Women’ using this song and our story to raise awareness for the abandonment problem in South Africa.
“We would really love our story to bring a light to this problem and to motivate people to get involved in whatever way they can”.

The situation
NGO’s like, Acres of Love , Impilo Place of Safety, Door of Hope, we would visit one ( filming the babies- strategically ie only showing backs of their heads), talk to the care givers and find out where their babies come from…..they have found children in tragic situations from inside a plastic bag to abandoned by the side of the river. What is the state of the babies when they find them, how do they care for them being so young and compromised.

Why is their a lack of accountability from the government re this issue, why are there no real figures re statistics of child abandonment, what we do know is it is in the thousands and increasing.
“If government took responsibility for this issue and addressed it on a national basis, we would know how many children are abandoned, when and where, and we could then put a strategy in place to solve this growing issue.”

Dee’s concern’s are the Governments “constructive prevention of adoption” through excessive red tape and lack of awareness so young women who are experiencing a crisis pregnancy do not know this is a viable alternative for them and more often than not they will leave it too late for a legal abortion so either have one too late or abandon

The Facts

There are no official stats on abandonment in South Africa but Child Welfare have estimated over 3 500 babies were abandoned in 2010 and all child protection experts believe that this number has increased in the last 5 years.

Gauteng mortuaries counted over 1 200 still births over 2012/2013, but ‘still births’ in hospitals are not sent to the morgue? When pushed morgue staff admitted that these “still births” were abandoned babies who were either premature or died of exposure when they were abandoned.

Police classify unnatural deaths into 3 categories murder, culpable homicide and inquests. Child abandonment are classified as inquests and are not reported in national crime statistics “It truly feels like a cover up”

In terms of the new Children’s Act a young woman can only place her child up for adoption when she turns 18, until this point she needs consent of parents or legal guardian however a child of any age can request an abortion at any state clinic or hospital.

An illegal immigrant is also unable to place her child in the formal child protection system in South Africa…she will be deported immediately.

What Dee has done
In Dee’s research she found that abandonment is the preferred choice to placing a baby/child up for adoption…60 % of children available for adoption were abandoned whilst less than 40% were formally placed up for adoption.

She has facilitated the formation of the National Adoption coalition for South Africa “adoption being the best long term solution for a child who has been abandoned by their biological parents or family”.
Developed an awareness campaign and national support centre for parents who want to adopt and for women experiencing a crisis pregnancy.
She has also developed a picture based global child protection community engagement programme aimed at empowering communities to deal proactively with the child protection challenges that they encounter every day (called Courage Child Protection see www.couragechildprotection.com)
 And at the end of last year developed a hard hitting child abandonment awareness campaign to try and get government to take responsibility for this growing national crisis.
Euphemism for stillborn – means abandoned baby in a mortuary

Press Release:


Abandoned Babies
It’s estimated that a staggering 3000 or more children are abandoned in South Africa every year. Whether left in public spaces to be found by Samaritans, or left to die unnoticed in squalor, accurate statistics are not recorded. So, how seriously does government view the plight of hundreds of these babies? Carte Blanche meets the heroes stepping in to give rescued little ones a new chance at life.


Script:


V/O 7 and a half sec
Jeremy Olivier’s heart rendering song written with his wife Nicole went viral within days of its release in 2014.

Up Song She lays him down in a field of pain/

V/O 7 sec
The song is about their adopted son, Noah who entered their life after Nicole miscarried, nearly dying in the process.

Jeremy: When Nicole was lying there It definitely changed my heart because before that I was not interested in adoption we have got four kids life is fine.

V/O 4 sec
A few weeks later they received an email from a friend about a baby who needed a home

Nicole: I read this out to Jeremy and next minute there were just tears welling out
Jeremy Tears welling out all of a sudden you have been through this really broken time and you have a softness that’s there that was not there before.

LINK
Noah was abandoned at birth left under a tree in a field he was wrapped in his mother’s jacket and hidden in a plastic bag

Jeremy: I said let’s go and see him, and we went to that safe house in Jeepers immediately this little guy was meant for us.
Nicole: He had this little yellow hat on and just this beautiful little face we had sat in this child welfare office with these angelic social workers and when we saw him I dunno something in us just went yes.

V/O 9 sec
There are no official statistics but Child Welfare South Africa estimated that in 2010 3 500 babies were abandoned…and that’s only the babies who survived.

Nicole: You hear the stories and I would just cry that could be Noah, I couldn’t picture him in a packet you know abandoned he just was my baby.

Dee: I saw a picture in a newspaper of a baby who had been abandoned on the outskirts of Soweto and she was dead and I was absolutely devastated

V/O 9 sec
A life changing moment for Dee Blackie, her biggest gripe, the lack of official statistics. How many babies a year are abandoned? How many don’t survive?

Dee: There is around ///over 1 000 in Gauteng mortuaries over the year of ‘ still births’ and if you speak to the morgue services they will tell you those are not still births those are in fact babies who have been found abandoned. In fact I spoke to the forensic head pathologist in the morgues and the comment to me was Dee we are swamped with dead babies every week.

V/O 4 sec
And in police reports there is no category for abandoned babies found dead.

Dee: So the police are not noting it because they note it down as an inquest they don’t note it down as abandonment or that this chid has been left to die,

V/O 13 sec
Connie Nxumalo, deputy director of the Department of Social Welfare says that while they don’t track stats of abandoned babies annually, they are included in a separate register with neglected and abused babies.

Devi: Why don’t we look at abandoned babies as a separate stat?
Connie: We don’t want to single out a single category we club them together to say these are children in need of care and protection in terms of our legislation.
Devi: We need the numbers because that may show a trend because the reality is whatever we are doing is not good enough?
Connie: I think you are right, we will try to mix separate desegregation within the child protection register So for me it’s just an IT programme not something we cannot do its something we can do.
Devi: I am so glad you said that because it’s easy to do so what’s stopping us doing it.
Connie: We are planning to do it.

Dee:, We have tried to lobby government at least let us understand who is abandoning, why are they abandoning because if we know that information we can start helping and stopping this thing from taking place.

V/O 10 sec
For every abandoned baby found alive it’s estimated there are two who have died. Desperate mothers will abandon in safe places and unsafe places. ….

Chriselda Bunu
Head of Adoptions at Johannesburg Child Welfare.
Chriselda: There are those that will drop children a drain, down a toilet. Some will abandon with milk and clothes. We have had one where the mother left a note to say please phone JHB Child Welfare on this number and they will take care of my child.

Nicole: I don’t believe his biological mother was meaning to throw him away..i think she was obviously overwhelmed.

UP SOUND SONG

V/O 7 sec
Nicole wrote these lyrics late one night thinking about the plight of Noah’s mother who found herself pregnant….

Nicole: I got a picture of this young girl feeling desperate and overwhelmed and afraid laying down this baby and as a mother how you what point of desperation you must be at to be able to put your baby down and walk away.

Devi: On the face of it doesn’t make sense because you can legally have an abortion in SA
Dee I think the more telling issue is why we have so many late abortions which is why we find a lot of the children in sewers in toilets because young girls are taking the medication which brings on contractions they are being told don’t worry the baby will dissolve inside you, the baby of course doesn’t dissolve and the baby is born premature and many of these babies in fact survive.

LINK
This is a baby bin in Yeoville Johannesburg where mothers deposit their unwanted babies there are many of these bins dotted across the country these bins save lives

LINK
The minute an infant is placed inside the baby bin here it triggers off a sensor, its also picked up on camera which relays into the house within minutes a care giver arrives and takes the baby.

V/O
Sadly Door of Hope is expanding due to the number of babies coming through their doors….and the challenges that hinder adoption.

Nadine: In the meantime these kids sit here when there are so many parents who want children its red tape that’s stopping them being adopted. … its really a sad situation /// the babies the innocent little children that had to go through a traumatic pregnancy and we see it first months that they are here///
Francine: the child will be screaming at night or maybe when you leave the child alone just showing the signs of trauma sometimes.

Dee: A lot of people blame the implementation of the children’s act, It’s actually a great piece of legislation its designed to protect the children, and to protect the birth mother and to protect the adoptive family, if you use it as a tool to facilitate adoption you have got no problems but if you use it as a tool to prevent adoptions you have all the checks and balances in place you can use to prevent an adoption taking place.

V/O 10 sec
And while you can negotiate an abortion at any age, you cant place your child up for adoption without family or a guardian’s consent until 18.

Chriselda: Younger than 18 they need to have a guardian accompanying them
Devi: That causes a problem most don’t want family to know
Chriselda: And that’s when you might find some young mother might resort to abandoning/// because they don’t want parents to know.

V/O 8 sec
Noah is now 6 years old and his adoption process went through without a hitch. Jeremy and Nicole have decided to be upfront and honest with Noah.

Nicole: we decided from the start we are just going to be honest and make it very natural and the n we started to talk about ..you didn’t come from Mommy’s tummy you were in another tummy but she was very scared and so she put you some where safe so Mummy and Daddy could find you, Now he understands a bit more he picks up things, but I think because he feels so secure and so loved ….he seems fine with it.

It all started for Dee when she saw picture in a newspaper of a little girl who had been abandoned and died on the outskirts of Soweto. Dee knew she had to do something. Approaching the government she was told:  “don’t understand” the problem ..I went back to university to do my masters in Anthropology looking child abandonment and adoption in the context of African ancestral beliefs. ….the abandoned Sindisiwe, whose name means ‘saved’ was abandoned by her mother in a hospital toilet, she was found by a nurse who thought she was dead, until miraculously Sindisiwe coughed and took her first breath. The nurse rushed her to the neonatal unit in the hospital and that is where she stayed for several months. Sindisiwe was eventually raised by her grandparents until they died when Sindisiwe was 12, and later by aunts. Sindisiwe never knew who her mother was until years later when she was an adult but on confronting her was “ I wish you had died then” Sindi, now in her 30’s, works as a charismatic minister ministering to people around the country. She is in the process of being ordained and setting up her own ministry. In Dee’s word’s “In her quiet unassuming way is an inspiration to many.” ….the saviours Nicole and Johan Olivier are a family of five, their youngest Noah was abandoned at birth, he was left under a tree in a field outside a township wrapped in a plastic bag inside his mother jacket. Nicole Olivier who had just miscarried twins got a call about Noah, for her it was meant to be. Love at first sight and three weeks later she adopted him, He is now the happiest and bubbliest 4 year old and the Olivier’s could not imagine their family without him.
metadata.Further information: “My husband, Jeremy, is a professional musician and singer-songwriter here in South Africa. We often write together, and about a year ago, we felt inspired to write about our story: how two tragic events have been turned into something so beautiful. “The response to this song has truly overwhelmed us. Jeremy has performed it on stages in Holland and Switzerland, as well as here in our own country and it seems to move people deeply. The Olivier’s work for UNICEF SA and the issue of abandoned babies is very close to their heart. “We are currently working with UNICEF SA on a new campaign called ‘Ending Violence Against Children and Women’ using this song and our story to raise awareness for the abandonment problem in South Africa. “We would really love our story to bring a light to this problem and to motivate people to get involved in whatever way they can”. The situation NGO’s like, Acres of Love , Impilo Place of Safety, Door of Hope, we would visit one ( filming the babies- strategically ie only showing backs of their heads), talk to the care givers and find out where their babies come from…..they have found children in tragic situations from inside a plastic bag to abandoned by the side of the river. What is the state of the babies when they find them, how do they care for them being so young and compromised. Why is their a lack of accountability from the government re this issue, why are there no real figures re statistics of child abandonment, what we do know is it is in the thousands and increasing. “If government took responsibility for this issue and addressed it on a national basis, we would know how many children are abandoned, when and where, and we could then put a strategy in place to solve this growing issue.” Dee’s concern’s are the Governments “constructive prevention of adoption” through excessive red tape and lack of awareness so young women who are experiencing a crisis pregnancy do not know this is a viable alternative for them and more often than not they will leave it too late for a legal abortion so either have one too late or abandon The Facts There are no official stats on abandonment in South Africa but Child Welfare have estimated over 3 500 babies were abandoned in 2010 and all child protection experts believe that this number has increased in the last 5 years. Gauteng mortuaries counted over 1 200 still births over 2012/2013, but ‘still births’ in hospitals are not sent to the morgue? When pushed morgue staff admitted that these “still births” were abandoned babies who were either premature or died of exposure when they were abandoned. Police classify unnatural deaths into 3 categories murder, culpable homicide and inquests. Child abandonment are classified as inquests and are not reported in national crime statistics “It truly feels like a cover up” In terms of the new Children’s Act a young woman can only place her child up for adoption when she turns 18, until this point she needs consent of parents or legal guardian however a child of any age can request an abortion at any state clinic or hospital. An illegal immigrant is also unable to place her child in the formal child protection system in South Africa…she will be deported immediately. What Dee has done In Dee’s research she found that abandonment is the preferred choice to placing a baby/child up for adoption…60 % of children available for adoption were abandoned whilst less than 40% were formally placed up for adoption. She has facilitated the formation of the National Adoption coalition for South Africa “adoption being the best long term solution for a child who has been abandoned by their biological parents or family”. Developed an awareness campaign and national support centre for parents who want to adopt and for women experiencing a crisis pregnancy. She has also developed a picture based global child protection community engagement programme aimed at empowering communities to deal proactively with the child protection challenges that they encounter every day (called Courage Child Protection see www.couragechildprotection.com)  And at the end of last year developed a hard hitting child abandonment awareness campaign to try and get government to take responsibility for this growing national crisis.
